staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, not the metadata vulnerable commit. All line anchors below use this container snapshot because it contains the vulnerable `translator2` reuse and matches the saved ASan trace.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42500245 (espeak-ng): Heap-use-after-free READ 4 found by fuzz target ssml-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42500245
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` in `TranslateLetter()` from the staged ARVO checkout `0a713d52bbf3e061823d1a7f35e5303e7320f27a`, whose vulnerable source differs from the metadata commit but matches the saved crash and patch hunk. On the witnessed path, `TranslateWord2()` takes its `phonSWITCH` branch, materializes an alternate-language token for the current word, and calls `SetTranslator2(new_language)` to install a word-level alternate translator. It then retranslates the same word through `TranslateWord(translator2, ...)`, so the active recursive translation frame holds that outer translator object in parameter `tr`. While spelling a letter from that word, `TranslateLetter()` decides the character must be spoken in yet another language and incorrectly reuses the same global `translator2` slot via `SetTranslator2(WordToString2(language))`. Because the nested language differs from the already installed outer word language, `SetTranslator2()` deletes the existing `translator2`, replaces the global with a new translator, and leaves the still-running outer `tr` alias dangling. `TranslateLetter()` later reaches `ph_buf[len+1] = tr->phoneme_tab_ix`, producing the saved heap-use-after-free read. The patch resolves this exact obligation by adding `translator3` and changing the nested `TranslateLetter()` language-switch operations to use that separate slot instead of clobbering the outer `translator2`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed vulnerable path that materializes the current word's alternate-language token from the input-derived `phonSWITCH` marker.
source.value_from: The saved allocation stack proves the enclosing `if (p[0] == phonSWITCH)` branch at `TranslateWord2:1484` was taken and then passed this token to `SetTranslator2()` at line 1495. Because runtime disambiguation is disabled and the 20-byte witness is non-ASCII, the exact token text is not recoverable from the saved static artifacts.

sink.description: ASan sink. The still-running outer `TranslateLetter()` frame reads `phoneme_tab_ix` through stale pointer `tr` after the nested `SetTranslator2()` path has freed that `Translator` object.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 4` at `numbers.c:839:26` on address `0x628000004258`, 344 bytes inside the 14864-byte region that the nested `SetTranslator2()` free stack had just released.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The nested letter-language switch reuses the shared global `translator2` slot even though the outer word translation is still using that same `Translator` object through parameter `tr`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds `translator3` and rewrites this nested `TranslateLetter()` path to call `SetTranslator3()` and use `translator3`, which prevents the inner language switch from freeing the outer word translator.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call aliases the live outer `translator2` object into the recursive word-translation stack as parameter `tr`. That alias survives after the nested `SetTranslator2()` free and is the pointer later dereferenced at the sink.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Step 2 installs global `translator2` for the word-level alternate language, and this call passes that same object by pointer into the later crashing `TranslateLetter()` frame.

parser_admitted.description: The witness word's initial pronunciation emitted a `phonSWITCH` marker, so `TranslateWord2()` entered its alternate-language retransliteration branch. The outer `translator2` object and the later UAF only arise on this path.

evidence_limitations: The staged vulnerable source snapshot is workspace commit `0a713d52bbf3e061823d1a7f35e5303e7320f27a`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `1f76c4b8bd320714aa61ad8abb527c5d92cc5164`. The staged checkout still reproduces the saved ASan crash and contains the same vulnerable `translator2` reuse fixed by `patch.diff`, so the trace is anchored to the staged line map.

Runtime disambiguation is disabled in `run_flags.json`, so the saved artifacts do not establish the exact alternate-language token text, the exact character/alphabet that made `TranslateLetter()` choose the nested-language branch, or whether the deeper `ph_buf[3] == phonSWITCH` subpath at lines 826-829 also executed. The trace records only the source-grounded facts proved by the executed lines 804 and 839 and by the saved ASan allocation/free stacks.

coarse_trace.summary: A word-level `phonSWITCH` marker materializes `new_language`, `SetTranslator2(new_language)` installs the outer alternate translator, and `TranslateWord(translator2, ...)` passes that object into the recursive translation stack as `tr`.
The retranslated word reaches the letter-by-letter fallback, and `TranslateLetter()` decides the current character must be spoken in another language while `tr` still aliases the outer `translator2`.

Nested `SetTranslator2(WordToString2(language))` reuses the shared `translator2` slot, detects a different language, frees the outer translator object, and installs a new global `translator2` for the inner letter lookup.
After the nested phoneme path produces a non-empty `ph_buf[3]`, the outer frame wraps that result and dereferences stale pointer `tr->phoneme_tab_ix`, triggering the ASan heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: Source. Inside the already-taken `if (p[0] == phonSWITCH)` branch, `TranslateWord2()` materializes the current word's alternate-language token from the input-derived switch marker. The saved allocation stack shows this token then flows directly into `SetTranslator2()` at line 1495. Because runtime disambiguation is disabled and the witness is non-ASCII, the exact token text is not recoverable from the saved artifacts.

The word-level language switch installs global `translator2` for `new_language`. ASan's allocation stack shows this call reaches `SelectTranslator()` and `NewTranslator()`, allocating the `Translator` object that is later freed and then read.

fine_trace.code:
wtab[0].flags |= FLAG_TRANSLATOR2;
flags = TranslateWord(translator2, word, wtab, &word_replaced[2]);
fine_trace.note: Because `switch_phonemes >= 0` on the witness, `TranslateWord2()` marks the word as being translated by `translator2` and passes that same object into the recursive call as parameter `tr`. The stale pointer later read at the sink is this outer-frame alias.

fine_trace.code: wordx += TranslateLetter(tr, wordx, unpron_phonemes, non_initial, current_alphabet);
fine_trace.note: On the witnessed path, `TranslateWord3()` enters the per-letter fallback and calls `TranslateLetter()` while `tr` still aliases the outer `translator2` from step 3. The saved crash stack records `TranslateWord3 / translate.c:777` directly above `TranslateLetter`, so this caller edge is part of the reproduced execution.

Inside `TranslateLetter()`, the current character/alphabet must be spoken in a language different from the outer translator, so the function takes its nested alternate-language branch. The saved free stack proves this predicate led to line 804 in the crashing execution, even though the exact letter and chosen language are not observable from the saved static artifacts.

Root cause. The nested letter-language switch reuses the shared global `translator2` slot even though the outer frame is still using that same `Translator` object through `tr`. The patch fixes this exact nested call by introducing `translator3` for `TranslateLetter()`.

Inside `SetTranslator2()`, the nested request is for a different language than the already-installed outer `translator2`, so the function takes its destructive reuse path instead of reusing the existing translator object.

The destructive reuse path frees the currently installed `translator2` object and clears the global. Because steps 3-5 passed that same object into the active outer translation frame as `tr`, the outer pointer becomes dangling here. ASan's free stack records `DeleteTranslator -> SetTranslator2 -> TranslateLetter` at this site.

After freeing the outer object, `SetTranslator2()` repopulates the global slot with a new `Translator` for the nested letter language and updates `translator2_language`. The still-running outer `tr` alias is not updated, so only the global now points to live state.

The nested lookup sequence under the rebound global `translator2` produced a non-empty phoneme string, so `TranslateLetter()` enters the block that appends a switch-back phoneme-table marker. The saved artifacts do not disambiguate whether this came directly from line 824 or from the deeper `ph_buf[3] == phonSWITCH` subpath at lines 826-829, and the trace does not claim more.

Sink. While wrapping the nested phoneme string, the outer frame dereferences `tr` after step 8 freed that `Translator`. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` at this exact line, 344 bytes inside the freed 14864-byte `Translator` region.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan allocation stack reaches `NewTranslator` because `TranslateWord2()` creates the outer word-level alternate translator with `SetTranslator2(new_language)` at this line.

free_context.note: The saved ASan free stack reaches `DeleteTranslator` because this nested `SetTranslator2()` call recycles the shared `translator2` slot while the outer frame still aliases it as `tr`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` adds `translator3`, factors alternate-translator setup into `SetAlternateTranslator()`, and changes the nested `TranslateLetter()` call sites from `SetTranslator2` / `translator2` to `SetTranslator3` / `translator3`. That keeps the outer word-level `translator2` alive while the inner letter-language switch runs.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: n/a: the initial outer translator allocation is valid; the lifetime bug is the later nested reuse of the same global `translator2` slot, which frees that live object while the outer frame still aliases it as `tr`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable reproduction ran `docker exec gt-arvo_42500245-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, fed this exact file to `ssml-fuzzer`, and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` in `TranslateLetter` with crash stack `TranslateLetter -> TranslateWord3 -> TranslateWord`.

format.name: raw ssml-fuzzer byte buffer
format.contract: Exactly the saved 20-byte witness `2a f3 ef b7 ba a0 81 90 9b d5 b7 d5 b7 d5 9b d5 bb ca b5 ff`. The harness copies those bytes verbatim, appends `\0`, and passes the result to `espeak_Synth(..., espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML)`. The saved artifacts prove only this witness and the resulting alternate-word-translator plus nested letter-language switch sequence; no broader text or language class is claimed.
